target_customer: Healthcare providers such as oncology clinics and revenue cycle teams doing intake, record abstraction and prior authorization
problem: Clinical and administrative staff spend hours reading medical records and handling intake and reimbursement paperwork.
business_model: B2B SaaS and AI automation with human review
product_category: AI document workflows and copilots for healthcare operations

founders.name: Ankit Ranjan
founders.background_notes: Listed as an engineer on the YC page.

competitors.name: Co:Helm
competitors.what: Health admin copilot for prior authorization

competitors.name: Basys.ai
competitors.traction_then: Launching with Mayo Clinic link per URL

technical_complexity.rationale: LLM extraction from varied clinical records with EHR integrations and HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance is demanding but standard for a small team in 2023 to 2024.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations and ground truth data from copilot use help, and it claims data from 76 percent of US oncology clinics, but this is an unsourced company claim and rivals were funded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TELCOR, an Accel-KKR backed revenue cycle software firm, acquired Sample in April 2026 with the team continuing in leadership roles.

market_need_then: Prior authorization and intake were widely cited administrative burdens with several startups seeded in 2023; no Sample specific demand figures were verified.

branding.domain_note: Uses samplehc.com, the company is also called Sample Healthcare, so the plain word domain was not used.

identity.visual_style: Standard SaaS marketing site with some unfinished template text
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, benefit focused with numeric claims

brand_strength.rationale: A generic common word that is hard to search for; no press about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Sample was a five person Winter 2024 healthcare AI company automating record abstraction, intake and prior authorization for clinics, with engineering rather than clinical founders. No funding was found publicly. In April 2026 TELCOR, owned by Accel-KKR, acquired it for undisclosed terms and the team stayed on, which suggests a strategic tuck in to a revenue cycle platform rather than a standalone venture outcome.
notes: No funding source found in a dedicated search; unknown, not zero. Website copy contains placeholder text and unsourced performance claims. Acquisition reported by Pulse 2.0, Preqin and Signalbase (close April 13, 2026); no TELCOR primary release seen. Competitor entries come from 2023 funding coverage; Basys.ai Mayo link is from the URL only.
